sources.entry: SPARDA by Zakaria Gharzouli (Residual Labs) - Converts a running Express or FastAPI app into an MCP server by AST-parsing its routes and injecting a marked, byte-for-byte-removable /mcp router, so the agent can operate your live application (real auth, real data) rather than just read files. Exceptionally safety-minded: writes are disabled by default behind two-phase confirmation, docstrings are s

summary.one_liner: SPARDA is a local, deterministic gate that compiles an Express, FastAPI, Flask, Next.js, NestJS or Medusa backend into a behavior graph, proves whether AI-written edits break guards or invariants, and can optionally inject an MCP server into the running app.
keywords: check ai generated code is safe
stop ai from removing auth checks
summary.what_it_does: Compiles a backend's routes, database queries, state mutations, guards and side-effects into one language-agnostic graph (UBG, stored as .sparda/ubg.json under the SBIR format). The apocalypse command checks that graph against five static obligations, including unguarded mutations, non-atomic aggregate writes, and unvalidated writes to constrained columns. The gate command diffs the graph before and after an edit and reports regressions such as a removed guard, with exit code 2 for use as a Claude Code PostToolUse hook. The init command scans routes via AST and injects a marked, reversible /mcp router that exposes the running app as MCP tools, with write tools disabled by default and two-phase confirmation. Other commands include timeless (record and replay requests), heal (gated self-repair), twin (safe simulated mock server), and mirror (serve the compiled graph over HTTP without the framework). The README says it runs locally with no API key and four exact-pinned runtime dependencies.
use_cases: check an ai-written backend edit before merging
block claude code edits that remove auth guards
run a safety check in ci with sarif output
expose a running express or fastapi app to an ai client as mcp tools
record a production request and replay it as a test
serve a mock backend for frontend development
notable: Two-phase write confirmation: enabled MCP write tools return a single-use token and preview first, and only commit after an explicit confirm step
Claude Code PostToolUse hook (gate --hook) that blocks edits removing a guard with exit code 2
Injected /mcp router is marked and removable byte-for-byte via npx sparda-mcp remove
Deterministic, offline graph verification with PROVEN (PARTIAL) and PREMISE NOT VERIFIED verdicts instead of false greens
Optional OpenAPI 3.x lowering to compile backends in other stacks such as Go, Java, Rails, Laravel, and .NET
caveats: README says most real apps come back NOT_PROVEN under the prover, and that partial coverage is reported as PARTIAL rather than full proof
Timeless replay is per-request only; concurrent-race capture is stated as out of scope for v1
OpenAPI lowering accepts JSON specs only in v1; YAML is not supported
Team features such as per-person access policies and a signed audit log are planned for a future paid tier; the README links to docs/SECURITY.md for known gaps
